text.p: Olympic champions the Netherlands thrashed England 6-0 to go top of the standings at the Golden Jubilee of Pakistan men's hockey tournament on Wednesday.
Apart from once losing 8-2 to Germany, it was the heaviest defeat suffered by England in over 100 years of playing internationals.
Yet England played a clever tactical game in the first half to restrict the Dutch to one goal, scored by Bram Lomans from a corner in the 29th minute.
But three minutes after the interval, Marten Eikelboom lobbed England's deputy goalkeeper Jimmi Lewis.
On either side of Eikelboom's goal, England squandered two golden chances, the second a rare penalty miss by their captain Russell Garcia who shot against an upright.

After that the Dutch swept through the England defence with brilliant inter-passing, scoring four goals in the last fifteen minutes, with Rochus Westbroek and their captain Stephan Veen each netting twice.
